subject: sub-11
notes: Manual ICA decisions after reviewing topographies and properties.

0.label: global_noise_component
0.notes: Diffuse bilateral frontal negativity with no clear dipolar structure — field extends uniformly across anterior scalp with weak posterior positivity. Not spatially smooth or dipolar enough. Noisy segment image with broadly distributed variance.

1.label: eye_blink_artifact
1.notes: Strong frontal positivity maximal at Fp1/Fp2 with posterior negativity — classic eye blink/EOG topography. Segment image shows persistent orange (positive) activity across upper segments consistent with EOG contamination. Reject.

2.label: edge_artifact
2.notes: Focal negativity concentrated at right posterior/temporal edge with no clear opposing pole inside the scalp. Not dipolar. Noisy 1/f spectrum with high variance. Edge-boundary distribution rules out neural source.

3.label: global_noise_component
3.notes: Broad anterior negativity with diffuse weak posterior positivity — not a clean dipole. Topography is spatially smeared and asymmetric. Segment image shows activity concentrated in early segments, possibly movement-related. Reject.

4.label: global_noise_component
4.notes: Entirely red topography covering the whole scalp with multiple irregular sign-change contours — clearly non-dipolar. Multiple focal hotspots visible. Consistent broadband noise. Reject.

5.label: global_noise_component
5.notes: Uniform diffuse negativity across entire scalp with no dominant pole or clear dipolar structure. Topography is essentially a flat blue field. Very weak signal. Reject.

6.label: mixed_component
6.notes: Focal right-central positivity embedded in broadly positive surround — not dipolar, no opposing negative pole. Topography appears to reflect a local hotspot rather than a dipolar source. Reject on strict criteria.

7.label: mixed_component
7.notes: Left-right asymmetric topography with right frontal positivity and left posterior negativity — could superficially suggest a dipole but orientation is oblique and irregular, not consistent with a clean neural dipole. Reject.

8.label: posterior_visual_component
8.notes: Right posterior/occipital focal positivity with broad anterior negativity — plausible dipolar structure consistent with a posterior visual source. Spectrum shows a clear alpha peak (~10 Hz) which strongly supports neural origin. Time course is continuous and well-behaved. Keep.

9.label: edge_artifact
9.notes: Focal high-amplitude positivity at left posterior-temporal/mastoid edge with no dipolar counterpart inside the scalp. Clearly an edge/electrode artifact. High variance outliers concentrated in mid-recording. Reject.

10.label: mixed_component
10.notes: Right fronto-central positivity with diffuse blue surround — partially dipole-like but the hot spot is too focal and the opposing field is too weak and non-smooth. Does not meet strict dipolar criteria for a clean neural source.

11.label: mixed_component
11.notes: Anterior positivity (fronto-temporal) with posterior negativity — superficially dipolar but asymmetric and the negative pole extends to the edge. Not consistent with a clean posterior neural source. Reject.

12.label: edge_artifact
12.notes: Focal left anterior/frontotemporal negativity concentrated near the edge with very weak opposing field. Not dipolar. Small isolated positive island at right front. Segment image suggests sporadic edge contamination.

13.label: global_noise_component
13.notes: Diffuse uniform negativity across entire scalp with no poles — essentially a DC/reference-like field. No dipolar structure whatsoever. Flat noisy spectrum. Reject.

14.label: posterior_visual_component
14.notes: Clear centro-parietal focal positivity with surrounding negativity — smooth, spatially well-defined, and dipolar. Spectrum shows a prominent alpha peak (~10 and ~20 Hz harmonics) strongly supporting neural origin. Clean, low-variance time course. Keep.

15.label: global_noise_component
15.notes: Broadly positive field covering right temporal and posterior regions with weak central negativity — not a clean dipole. Multiple irregular contours. No dominant alpha peak in spectrum. Reject.

16.label: mixed_component
16.notes: Central blue focus surrounded by red — ring-like topography that does not correspond to a dipolar neural source. This pattern is commonly seen in reference artifacts or non-dipolar mixing. Reject.

17.label: posterior_visual_component
17.notes: Left parieto-occipital focal positivity with surrounding negativity — smooth and dipolar, consistent with a lateral posterior visual or parietal source. Spectrum shows clear alpha (~10 Hz) and beta peaks. Well-behaved continuous time course. Keep.

18.label: posterior_visual_component
18.notes: Left centro-parietal focal positivity with smooth blue surround — dipolar and spatially clean. Spectrum has a clear 1/f slope with alpha peak. Topography is consistent with a parietal/posterior neural source. Time course is stable. Keep.

19.label: temporal_muscle_artifact
19.notes: Bilateral lateral positivity at left and right temporal/mastoid edges with central negativity — classic bilateral temporal muscle or reference artifact pattern. Not dipolar. Step-like deflection in time course. Extreme variance outlier. Reject.

20.label: mixed_component
20.notes: Central-parietal negativity embedded in a broadly positive field — not a clean dipole. The negative pole is spatially isolated and asymmetric with no well-defined opposing positive counterpart. Noisy time course and scattered variance. Reject.

21.label: posterior_visual_component

22.label: posterior_visual_component
22.notes: Right parieto-occipital focal positivity with broad surrounding negativity — smooth and well-defined dipolar pattern consistent with a lateral posterior visual source. Spectrum shows clear alpha (~10 Hz) and beta peaks. Stable time course. Keep.
